root_cause.text: The IRQ handler in dpaa2-switch uses a hardware-provided if_id (0-65535) to index into ethsw->ports[] without verifying that it is within the allocated array size (sw_attr.num_ifs), leading to a potential out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `if (if_id >= ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs)` before accessing `ethsw->ports[if_id]`, and the CVE description states that "if_id can be any 16-bit value (0-65535) but the ports array is only allocated with sw_attr.num_ifs elements".

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The IRQ handler in dpaa2-switch uses a hardware-provided if_id (0-65535) to index into ethsw->ports[] without verifying that it is within the allocated array size (sw_attr.num_ifs), leading to a potential out-of-bounds read.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds a bounds check `if (if_id >= ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs)` before accessing `ethsw->ports[if_id]`, and the CVE description states that "if_id can be any 16-bit value (0-65535) but the ports array is only allocated with sw_attr.num_ifs elements".

candidates.rationale: Extracts the hardware-provided if_id without bounds checking, making it an untrusted index.
Uses the unverified if_id to index into the fixed-size array ethsw->ports[], causing an out-of-bounds read when if_id exceeds sw_attr.num_ifs.
This condition entry leads to further dereferences of port_priv without prior validation of the index, assuming the OOB read did not cause a fault.

vuln_statements.explanation: Extracts the hardware-provided if_id from the status register without any bounds check. This if_id (0-65535) is later used as an array index, making it the source of the untrusted index.
Directly indexes into ethsw->ports[] using the unverified if_id, causing an out-of-bounds read if if_id >= sw_attr.num_ifs. This is the core vulnerable statement.

This conditional branch dereferences port_priv without any previous index validation. If the OOB read resulted in a non-NULL pointer, the subsequent code could access invalid memory, making this statement part of the vulnerable execution path.
